Traffic Advisory

A walkathon for Har Ghar Tiranga -2025 on dated 14.08.2025 from Kamla Market to Central park Connaught Circus, Delhi will include the participation of approximately 5000 students. The route of the walkathon is Hamdard Chowk, Round About Kamla Market, Minto Road, Ajmeri Gate Chowk, Bhavbhuti Marg, Sarvodya Kanya Vidhyalalya R.S. Flyover, Press Cut, Tagore Road Red Light, Mata Sundari College, DDU Marg, Minto Road Light and Enter Connaught Circus.

DIVERSION / RESTRICTION-

There will be diversion / restriction on Hamdard Chowk, Round About Kamla Market, Minto Road, Ajmeri Gate Chowk, Bhavbhuti Marg, R.S. Flyover, Tagore Road Red Light, Mata Sundari College, DDU Marg, Minto Road Light. No heavy vehicles and buses shall be allowed on these roads. Commuters are requested to avoid following roads on 14.08.2025 from 9.30AM to 12 PM on the day of walkathon.

PARKING-

There is no parking facility available at Mata Sundari Road.
There is no parking for general public.

GENERAL VEHICLE-

No vehicles shall be allowed to be parked on Ajmeri Gate Chowk, Bhavbhuti Marg, DDU, JLN Marg and Minto Road (Both the carriageways) on the day of walkathon. Vehicles parked on these roads shall be towed away and prosecuted as per law.

data.raw_text:
August 14

Week-long ‘Ondoy,’ ‘Carina’ level rain contributed to Metro Manila flooding — solon

SURIGAO del Sur 1st District Rep. Romeo Momo Sr. on late Wednesday afternoon said the massive rainfall that hit Metro Manila from July 19 to 25—comparable in volume to Typhoons “Ondoy” and “Carina”—was a major factor behind the recent flooding, with nearly one-third of the capital’s annual average rainfall falling in just seven days.

Citing data from the Effective Flood Control Operation System of the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA), Momo said the week-long rains totaled 665.5 millimeters, or 28 percent of Metro Manila’s yearly average.

“Ibig sabihin sa period ng isang linggo, one-third of the annual average rainfall in Metro Manila binuhos lamang ng isang linggo na ulan,” Momo told the House Committee on Public Accounts chaired by Bicol Saro Party-list Rep. Terry Ridon during a briefing by the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) on flood control projects and efforts to address Metro Manila’s flooding problem.

“Lagi kasi nating sinisisi ang flood control, ‘di rin natin tinitingnan kung gaano ang volume na pumasok sa mga flood control systems ng MMDA at DPWH,” Momo added.

Committee chair Bicol Saro Party-list Rep. Terry Ridon asked if the nearly week-long rainfall matched “Ondoy” and “Carina” levels and if it had overwhelmed the country’s flood control systems.

PAGASA Deputy Administrator Engr. Roy A. Badilla said “Ondoy” and “Carina” brought intense, short bursts of rain, while the recent weather disturbance “Crising” delivered the same total over a longer period, allowing partial drainage before peak rainfall.

Even so, Momo said the week’s rainfall equaled a 100-year return period, as confirmed by DPWH Project Manager Jerry Fano, who noted that “Crising’s” rainfall matched this threshold based on PAGASA’s intensity-duration-frequency curve.

On further questioning, Fano admitted that Metro Manila’s drainage systems are designed for only a 15-year return period, upgraded from 10 years in 2005 to account for climate change.

“You can just imagine ang buhos ng ulan 100-year return period, but the capacities of our drainage system is only 15-year return period. Saan papunta ang mga tubig na ‘yan kundi mag-overflow talaga,” Momo said.

Momo said the mismatch explains why Metro Manila experiences frequent flooding and urged the full implementation of the Metro Manila Flood Management Master Plan to upgrade all drainage systems.

The briefing reviewed the performance of the DPWH’s Unified Project Management Office–Flood Control Cluster and received updates on ongoing and planned flood control projects.

It was part of the response of the House, under Speaker Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez, to President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s call in his State of the Nation Address (SONA) to combat corruption, substandard work, and “ghost” projects, underscored by recent widespread flooding in Luzon.
